title: Reflections on the Early Days of Reserve Management Purchases and the Maintenance of Ample Reserves

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: Federal Reserve SOMA Manager Roberto Perli delivered remarks on the transition from abundant to ample reserves, explaining that the FOMC decided at its October 2025 meeting to conclude balance sheet runoff effective December 1, and subsequently instructed the Desk to begin reserve management purchases (RMPs) to maintain reserves within the ample range. Perli detailed how system liquidity fell to the lowest levels since runoff began due to TGA rebuild and cumulative balance sheet reduction, causing repo rates to rise sustainably above EFFR and triggering increased usage of standing repo operations.
key_points: The FOMC concluded SOMA securities runoff at its October 2025 meeting, effective December 1, after determining reserve balances were approaching the ample range.
Reserve management purchases (RMPs) began in December 2025 when the FOMC judged that reserves had declined to the ample range.
The Treasury General Account (TGA) rebuild after the debt limit increase in early July 2025, combined with balance sheet runoff, reduced system liquidity to the lowest levels since QT began.
ON RRP usage declined to de minimis levels by October 2025, reducing the pool of funds available to shift into private repo and causing repo rates to rise above EFFR.
EFFR rose from 7 basis points to 1 basis point under IORB from mid-September through November 2025, faster than observed in early 2018 during the previous balance sheet runway period.
The FOMC defines ample reserves as the range where the federal funds rate is only modestly sensitive to short-term variations in reserve supply.
why_it_matters: This speech provides authoritative first-hand perspective on the Federal Reserve's operational framework for managing reserves in an ample regime. It documents the technical transition from quantitative tightening to reserve management purchases, which has direct implications for money market dynamics, repo market functioning, and the effective federal funds rate. Market participants need to understand these dynamics as they affect funding costs, collateral allocation, and the transmission of monetary policy through short-term markets.
market_structure_context: The speech comprehensively describes the transition from abundant to ample reserves, including detailed indicator frameworks for monitoring reserve conditions. It explains how FHLBs connected repo and federal funds markets, how ON RRP decline affected repo rate dynamics, and how SRP usage became larger and more frequent as conditions tightened. The SOMA Manager discusses the mechanics of RMP implementation and the factors influencing reserve supply, providing a rare operational deep-dive into Fed balance sheet management.
important_numbers: 7 basis points (EFFR spread above IORB in mid-September 2025)
1 basis point (EFFR under IORB by November 2025)
December 1, 2025 (effective date for concluding SOMA runoff)
October 2025 (FOMC meeting where runoff conclusion decided)
July 2025 (debt limit increase, TGA rebuild began)
notes: Source body was truncated in the provided text; only approximately two-thirds of the speech was visible. The key content on reserve adequacy indicators and the role of standing repo operations in the conclusion could not be captured. The speech was delivered March 26, 2026, making it recent and highly relevant. The speech was given before the Money Marketeers of New York University. Perli explicitly notes these are his own views, not official Fed positions. Speaker is a senior official with direct operational responsibility for implementing monetary policy.
